1.why: All eight screens show a static single-card layout with no animations, moving images, or modal pop-ups.

2.why: Primary buttons are solid teal, secondary buttons are outlined, headings are bold, and notices use green/amber highlight boxes, so key elements visually stand out.

3.why: Each screen presents one task with a single input and one clear primary button, making the needed element quick to locate.

4.why: The password rule is printed on the page, the reset token arrives pre-filled, and the one-time code stays visible in the Logs panel, so little must be memorized.

5.why: No 'remember me' checkbox, autofill option, or password-manager integration is visible on any screen.

6.why: The pre-filled token field and codes remaining visible in the Logs panel support recognition, but no saved logins or familiar items are offered.

7.why: Instructions are brief and plain-language, though demo jargon like 'simulated recovery message' and 'Logs panel and browser console' slightly reduces clarity.

8.why: No error messages appear in any of the eight steps; only success and neutral status messages are shown.

9.why: No placeholder examples or sample passwords are provided, though the pre-filled token field demonstrates what to paste.

10.why: The system offers only one fixed path (email token, new password, one-time code); no password/code/face login alternatives are presented.

11.why: Every screen shows at most one input field and one to three buttons, so the user never faces many choices at once.

12.why: A green confirmation follows the reset request and a 'Conditions accepted' page confirms completion, but mid-flow steps advance without explicit success messages.

13.why: Each step includes a short guidance sentence and early screens show a 'Stay safe' tip box, though no dedicated help link or support option exists.

14.why: A 'Back' button exists on the token step, but no retry, resend-code, or error-recovery path is demonstrated.

15.why: All eight screens reuse the identical header, card container, typography, color scheme, and button styles throughout the flow.
